metadata.schedule_summary: Both chemotherapy medicines are planned on Day 1 of a 21-day cycle. For pleural mesothelioma, the source describes up to 4–6 cycles. For advanced non-squamous NSCLC, it describes 4–6 combination cycles followed, when appropriate, by a separate pemetrexed maintenance plan (NCCP00222). The selected preoperative nivolumab combination uses three cycles and a separate immunotherapy plan (NCCP00849). Your team confirms which course applies and may stop or change it earlier.

indications.description: First-line treatment of locally advanced or metastatic non-small cell lung cancer.
With nivolumab for neoadjuvant treatment of resectable NSCLC at high risk of recurrence with PD-L1 expression ≥1% (3 cycles).
Unresectable mesothelioma, non-squamous NSCLC or selected neoadjuvant NSCLC.

treatment_phases.label: Day 1 chemotherapy in a 21-day cycle
notes: Pemetrexed then cisplatin. Cisplatin starts 30 minutes after pemetrexed; pre/post hydration under local policy.

Mesothelioma: maximum 4–6 cycles; advanced NSCLC: 4–6 cycles then separately assessed pemetrexed maintenance NCCP00222 if appropriate; neoadjuvant nivolumab context: three cycles with separate NCCP00849 plan.

diarrhoea_grade.label: Diarrhoea grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No increase above the patient's usual stool frequency or ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Increase of fewer than 4 stools per day above baseline, or mild increase in ostomy output.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Increase of 4–6 stools per day above baseline, or moderate increase in ostomy output; limits instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Increase of 7 or more stools per day above baseline, incontinence, hospital care indicated, or severe ostomy-output increase; limits self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

diarrhoea_grade.assessment_guidance: Count stools per day above the patient's baseline, assess ostomy output, continence, hydration, fever, abdominal pain, haemodynamic compromise and whether hospital care is indicated.

mucositis_grade.label: Mucositis grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No oral mucositis.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Asymptomatic or mild symptoms; intervention not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate pain or ulceration that does not interfere with oral intake; modified diet indicated.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe pain that interferes with oral intake.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

mucositis_grade.assessment_guidance: Inspect the oral cavity and assess pain, ulceration, diet modification and whether oral intake is impaired.

neuropathy_grade.label: Neurotoxicity grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No peripheral sensory or motor neuropathy.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Asymptomatic; clinical or diagnostic observations only. CTCAE v5.0 grades symptomatic paraesthesia separately when that is the more accurate term.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Moderate symptoms that limit instrumental activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Severe symptoms that limit self-care activities of daily living.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening neurological consequences; urgent intervention required.

neuropathy_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess sensory and/or motor symptoms and their effect on instrumental versus self-care activities of daily living. Distinguish transient cold sensitivity from persistent functional neuropathy.

other_toxicity_grade.label: Other non-haematologic toxicity grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No other non-haematological adverse event.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Grade 1 under the named CTCAE term: generally mild or asymptomatic, with observation only and no intervention indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Grade 2 under the named CTCAE term: generally moderate; local/non-invasive intervention may be indicated and instrumental activities may be limited.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Grade 3 under the named CTCAE term: severe or medically significant; hospital care may be indicated and self-care activities may be limited.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Grade 4 under the named CTCAE term: life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

other_toxicity_grade.assessment_guidance: Name the exact non-haematological adverse event first and apply that event's own CTCAE v5.0 criterion. The general Grade 1-4 severity anchors are a screening aid only and are not a substitute for the named term.

allergic_reaction_grade.label: Allergic reaction grade

options.label: Grade 0
options.description: No allergic reaction.

options.label: Grade 1
options.description: Systemic intervention is not indicated.

options.label: Grade 2
options.description: Oral intervention is indicated.

options.label: Grade 3
options.description: Bronchospasm, hospitalisation for clinical sequelae, or IV intervention is indicated.

options.label: Grade 4
options.description: Life-threatening consequences; urgent intervention required.

allergic_reaction_grade.assessment_guidance: Assess whether systemic treatment is required, route of treatment, bronchospasm, angioedema, hypotension, hospitalisation and life-threatening features. If the event is infusion-related, use the CTCAE infusion-related reaction term rather than double-reporting both.

monitoring: Baseline FBC, renal and liver profile; audiology if clinically indicated. Review cisplatin hydration/electrolytes and baseline renal suitability.
Repeat FBC, renal and liver profile before each cycle. Review infection, bleeding, gastrointestinal toxicity, neuropathy, hearing and medicines.
Disease assessment and additional tests follow the consultant treatment plan; no universal scan interval is specified.
dose_modifications: Source count thresholds use current pretreatment counts; nadir wording was removed in the October 2025 source update.
All dose modifications require consultant discussion. Previous-dose adverse-event percentages are not automatically applied to the original protocol doses.
